title: [bug]  SEA - Unknown arguments: max-old-space-size, maxOldSpaceSize

triage_metadata.reasoning: scripts/build_binary.js was pruned because its changes (setting file executable permissions on the target binary and passing '--yes' to 'npx' during postject execution) are build script adjustments and not source code required to resolve the runtime Node.js argument parsing bug in SEA mode.

summary.problem: When running Gemini CLI as a Single Executable Application (SEA), Node.js runtime arguments (such as --max-old-space-size) passed during process relaunch are treated as command-line arguments and passed to yargs, causing an 'Unknown arguments: max-old-space-size, maxOldSpaceSize' error.
summary.root_cause: During child process relaunch, Node.js flags like auto-configured memory flags were being appended to command-line arguments passed to spawn(process.execPath, ...). In SEA mode, process.execPath is the executable binary itself, which forwards all command-line arguments directly to the application parser (yargs) rather than consuming them as Node.js runtime flags.
summary.context: SEA mode requires Node.js options to be passed via the NODE_OPTIONS environment variable during relaunch rather than as CLI arguments. Additionally, relaunching SEA processes requires distinct process.argv slicing (isStandardSea vs relaunch child) and injecting process.execPath as the argv[1] script placeholder to maintain the [node, script, ...args] format and prevent argument compounding.

steps: In packages/cli/src/utils/processUtils.ts, export functions isStandardSea(), getScriptArgs(), isSeaEnvironment(), and getSpawnConfig(nodeArgs, scriptArgs) along with the ProcessWithSea interface.
Implement isStandardSea() to return true when process.argv[0] !== process.argv[1] and either process.env.IS_BINARY === 'true' or process.isSea?.() === true.
Implement getScriptArgs() to slice process.argv starting at index 1 if isStandardSea() is true, and index 2 otherwise.

Implement getSpawnConfig(nodeArgs, scriptArgs) to detect SEA mode via isSeaEnvironment(). In SEA mode, validate nodeArgs for invalid characters (spaces, quotes, backslashes), append nodeArgs to NODE_OPTIONS in newEnv, and set spawnArgs to [process.execPath, ...scriptArgs]. In standard Node mode, set spawnArgs to [...process.execArgv, ...nodeArgs, process.argv[1], ...scriptArgs].

In packages/cli/index.ts and packages/cli/src/utils/relaunch.ts, replace custom process.argv slicing and manual child process spawn argument construction with calls to getScriptArgs() and getSpawnConfig().

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When relaunching in SEA binary mode, memory and runtime Node flags are passed through NODE_OPTIONS instead of command-line arguments, preventing yargs unknown argument errors and argument compounding.
verification_steps: Add unit tests for isStandardSea, getScriptArgs, isSeaEnvironment, and getSpawnConfig covering standard Node mode and SEA mode.
Verify that getSpawnConfig populates NODE_OPTIONS when IS_BINARY is set and uses process.execPath as the script placeholder in spawnArgs.
Verify that getSpawnConfig throws an error if complex or unescaped arguments are passed to nodeArgs in SEA mode.
Run tests using Vitest to confirm processUtils and relaunch utilities pass.

golden_spec_rationale: scripts/build_binary.js was pruned because its changes (setting file executable permissions on the target binary and passing '--yes' to 'npx' during postject execution) are build script adjustments and not source code required to resolve the runtime Node.js argument parsing bug in SEA mode.
